candidates.passage: In the line with increasing demand outlook and strong customer traction in the US oilfield chemicals market, we are now in process of doubling the manufacturing capacity in CrudeChem. This expansion positions helps us to cater to larger contracts, onboard new customers and accelerate growth in the high-margin specialty oilfield chemicals segment.
candidates.speaker: Aarti Jhunjhunwala, Executive Director
candidates.adjudication_note: Capacity doubling of CrudeChem (US subsidiary) is in progress ('now in process of') but NO completion date is stated in this turn. On page 6 management notes capacity is being increased 'from December onwards' with machines 'installing in a couple of weeks', and ties peak capacity to the $200M revenue target. As written it FAILS Gate 1's timeframe requirement — included per over-propose. Adjudicator: cut unless a firm doubling-completion date is verified.

candidates.passage: At the same time, the EBITDA margins have been improving considerably with the, kind of, the resources, which we have -- after our -- after we being the shareholders in CrudeChem, we could have a lot more resources on machinery, manpower, negotiations and suppliers’ negotiations. So, these factors have contributed to increase of EBITDA. So going forward, I think comfortably, we should be at EBITDA of 15% more or less.
candidates.speaker: Sanjay Tibrewala, CFO
candidates.adjudication_note: This is the CCT / US Oil & Gas business EBITDA ('as we scale up the business'), NOT the consolidated figure — distinct from the 18–20% blended number given later (candidates 5–6). 'Going forward' carries no firm timeframe — verify Gate 1 timeframe and horizon.

candidates.passage: I think easily, we should be looking at touching a business of $200 million with the new investment we are going to do in the machineries. [...] So, we are totally geared about it. Earlier, our expectation to touch $200 million was something in 2030. However, I think that should not take so long now. It should be definitely before 2028. So this is the kind of action going on.
candidates.speaker: Sanjay Tibrewala, CFO
candidates.adjudication_note: CCT/CrudeChem (US subsidiary) revenue target, USD-denominated, hence level=segment and not scorable against Screener INR consol P&L. Originally introduced by analyst Amit Mehendale citing the PPT ('Are we expecting $200 million of revenue in FY 26... in FY ’28?') and accepted by management, who gave the timeframe 'before 2028' (revised down from an earlier 2030 expectation). Current annualized run-rate cited as ~$90–100M. Verify whether '2028' is calendar or fiscal year. See also candidate 4.

candidates.passage: Darshil Jhaveri: Yes. Hi, sir. So, sir, just wanted to understand with the $200 million target that we have from CCT business itself, what is the revenue guidance that we could give for FY '27 and FY '28? [...] Sanjay Tibrewala: So we also revised, we were planning $200 million business in 2030, which is now revised to 2028 because also a lot of our technology transfers have also been done from Fineotex, a lot of products are going to be produced and already being produced in US where the market is.
candidates.speaker: Sanjay Tibrewala, CFO
candidates.adjudication_note: Near-duplicate of candidate 3 (the $200M CCT target). Kept because it explicitly confirms the revision 2030 -> 2028. Note management declined to give a specific consolidated FY27/FY28 revenue number in the same answer ('I would not be able to share any forward-looking statements here').

candidates.passage: On a blended level, we would always look at getting to an easy EBITDA of around 18% to 20%, and that's what we are heading to. I think it's not too far from now, but what's more important right now is to drive the businesses and take the maximum businesses in control, and then keep working on the operational EBITDAs and operational efficiencies. [...] So, I can easily envisage that 18% to 20% blended should be easy, should be achievable by us.
candidates.speaker: Sanjay Tibrewala, CFO
candidates.adjudication_note: KEY company-level scorable item (consol blended EBITDA, Q4 FY26 consol was ~14%). The 18–20% figure originates with management here; the FY27 timeframe is firmed by analyst exchanges later: Keshv Garg (page 11) frames 'for FY ’27 itself... 18% to 20%' and management says 'eventually we'll be targeting and touching the blended EBITDA'; Vinay Nadkarni (page 14) asks 'F27 or F28' and management answers 'even in this financial year' (= FY27). Hedged language ('not too far from now', 'eventually') means the FY27 pin and therefore horizon=near / credibility_scorable=true should be verified. If the firm year is FY28, retag horizon=medium and credibility_scorable=false.

candidates.passage: Vinay Nadkarni: Great. I think it's a great acquisition. Just one last question for you. When you said 18% to 20% of blended EBITDA going forward, would that be in F '27 or would you look at that as F '28? [...] Sanjay Tibrewala: We are trying our best to make it as soon as – as quickly as possible, but I think this can be reflecting even in this financial year. So, I won't be surprised rather on that.
candidates.speaker: Sanjay Tibrewala, CFO
candidates.adjudication_note: Timeframe-confirmation turn for the 18–20% blended/consolidated EBITDA target (candidate 5). Analyst-originated F27-vs-F28 framing, management accepts F27 ('even in this financial year' from a May-2026 call = FY27, Apr 2026–Mar 2027). Near-duplicate of candidate 5, kept to anchor the timeframe verbatim. Commitment is mildly hedged ('trying our best', 'can be reflecting').

candidates.passage: Coming to your different question about the stake. So, yes, we have already signed with the founders that further 25% has to be sold by them to Finotech’s in January '28. It's part of the agreement. So that's about it. So that is going to add us to almost 79% or 80%.
candidates.speaker: Sanjay Tibrewala, CFO
candidates.adjudication_note: Binary corporate-action commitment: contracted purchase of a further 25% of CCT from the founders in January 2028, taking Fineotex's stake from 53% to ~79–80%. Clearly falsifiable (completed or not by Jan 2028). Novel metric name — reconcile with vocabulary. Level tagged 'company' (ownership), but it concerns the CCT subsidiary; adjudicator may prefer level=segment. ('Finotech’s' is the transcript's spelling of Fineotex.)

candidates.passage: Going forward, I think with Fineotex organic growth, the kind of -- last year, we had a new plant investment in India, which is in Ambernath, plus we have the CCT now with us. I don't feel a challenge that it can go another 3, 4 times in the next 4 years or something like that. So this is something which is within the range. And I think we will be looking at it.
candidates.speaker: Sanjay Tibrewala, CFO
candidates.adjudication_note: PRIMARY long-horizon re-rating signal. Management: revenue can 'go another 3, 4 times in the next 4 years.' Implied CAGR ~32–41%. 'Next 4 years' from the May-2026 (FY26) call ≈ FY30 — verify base/target year. Novel metric (multiple, not a level or %). Closely related to the INR3,000cr framing accepted two turns later (candidate 9).

candidates.passage: Nalin Shah: You said it could be 3 to 4 times from the present. So can we assume -- I mean, very, very reasonably speaking, that in 3 to 4 years' time, we could be a INR3,000 crores top line company from here? [...] Sanjay Tibrewala: Oh yes. That if the way the things are going on, I would not be at all surprised if we don't -- I mean, touching that number will -- I mean, I will be rather surprised if we don't touch it.
candidates.speaker: Sanjay Tibrewala, CFO
candidates.adjudication_note: Analyst-originated (Nalin Shah), management-EXPLICITLY-accepted INR3,000 crore consolidated top-line target in 3–4 years ('I will be rather surprised if we don't touch it'). The rupee-denominated counterpart of the 3–4x aspiration (candidate 8). Aspirational long-horizon, consol-level → not scorable. Verify target year (FY29 vs FY30).

candidates.passage: And as you rightly said that Q4 is establishing the benchmark for the future, so in the light of that, I would say, broadly, we come to the number that your top line could be in the vicinity of about INR1,200 crores, INR1,250 crores and bottom line could be something like INR175 crores, INR185 crores. This is my second question.
candidates.speaker: Nalin Shah, NVS Brokerage (analyst — proposed, not confirmed by management)
candidates.adjudication_note: Analyst-PROPOSED consolidated top line ~INR1,200–1,250cr. Management did NOT explicitly confirm — Sanjay deflected ('the quarter 4 numbers are the base numbers... a lot of things which are going to happen even this year'). Likely FAILS Gate 1's management-acceptance bar for analyst-originated figures → probable CUT. Timeframe also unclear (Nalin framed 'next 3 years' but ~INR1,250cr ≈ Q4 FY26 annualized run-rate, implying FY27). If you judge management accepted it as near-term consol revenue, it would become credibility_scorable=true — hence flagged, not dropped.

candidates.passage: And as you rightly said that Q4 is establishing the benchmark for the future, so in the light of that, I would say, broadly, we come to the number that your top line could be in the vicinity of about INR1,200 crores, INR1,250 crores and bottom line could be something like INR175 crores, INR185 crores. This is my second question.
candidates.speaker: Nalin Shah, NVS Brokerage (analyst — proposed, not confirmed by management)
candidates.adjudication_note: Same passage and caveat as candidate 10: analyst-PROPOSED bottom line ~INR175–185cr, not explicitly accepted by management. Likely CUT. Split out as a separate metric (PAT) from the revenue figure.

candidates.passage: Rohit Ohri: So on a steady state, then CrudeChem can give us somewhere around INR600 crores, INR650 crores kind of a top line, right? [...] Sanjay Tibrewala: Yes, easily. There's no doubt about it.
candidates.speaker: Sanjay Tibrewala, CFO
candidates.adjudication_note: Analyst-originated (Rohit Ohri), management-accepted ('Yes, easily') CrudeChem steady-state top line ~INR600–650cr. BUT 'steady state' is a condition, not a date — likely FAILS Gate 1's timeframe requirement. Tension with the $200M (≈INR1,700cr) CCT target: 600–650cr ≈ current Q4 annualized run-rate (CCT Q4 ~INR165–170cr), so this may be a near-term run-rate confirmation rather than a forward target. Verify intended timeframe before keeping.

candidates.passage: So there has been a lot of capex being done. In fact, after the acquisition also, the Fineotex has already done a capex of around $7 million. And, I mean, Fineotex has extended the funds to CCT for investments further of almost -- the line of -- this thing is almost $7 million. So, yes, this is going on.
candidates.speaker: Sanjay Tibrewala, CFO
candidates.adjudication_note: ~$7M already spent post-acquisition (backward-looking) PLUS a further funding line of ~$7M extended to CCT for investment (forward, but NO timeframe). Muddled phrasing. As stated it likely FAILS Gate 1 (no date; partly past) → probable CUT, or keep only the forward $7M line if a timeframe can be verified.

candidates.passage: And the companies, is rather -- even if I talk to you, even if you talk about the wallet share, I can -- I would like to make this statement here. The wallet share increase with the kind of customers we have right now, forget about adding more customers, can easily go to 5x. [...] So rather, even if you don't get any new customers, I'm just saying hypothetically, with the same customers, we have a potential of going 5x because they are giant companies.
candidates.speaker: Sanjay Tibrewala, CFO
candidates.adjudication_note: Explicitly hypothetical ('I'm just saying hypothetically') 5x wallet-share potential with existing CCT customers. NO timeframe and not a standard financial metric (wallet share, not revenue/margin) — almost certainly FAILS Gate 1. Included only per the over-propose instruction; adjudicator should very likely CUT.
